newsitem.title: USA: Food industry investigation continues -- Justice.
newsitem.headline: Food industry investigation continues -- Justice.

text.p: The Justice Department said Tuesday its investigation into the food and feed additives industry, including high-fructose corn syrup (HFCS), was still active.

Archer Daniels Midland Co had agreed to cooperate with the investigation as part of an agreement to plead guilty to charges of price fixing in the lysine and citric acid markets, Attorney General Janet Reno said.
Although ADM will not plead guilty to charges relating to the HFCS market, the firm must cooperate with the investigation into that market, Reno said.

Reno was speaking at a news conference officially announcing that ADM had agreed to pay a $100-million fine, the largest criminal antitrust fine ever, for its role in international price-fixing conspiracies.

The agreement assures ADM and all but two of its executives will not be prosecuted further in the investigation. The non-prosecution assurance includes the HFCS market, Deputy Assistant Attorney General Gary Spratling said.
Spratling declined to say why ADM would plead guilty to the lysine and citric acid price fixing, but not to allegations concerning the bigger HFCS market.
